penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: CAD-to-mesh conversion at acceptable quality requires running specialized geometry kernels (Open CASCADE, Parasolid SDK, or equivalent) and per-model QA — Claude cannot perform this; every conversion job needs validated toolchain execution and likely manual mesh inspection for complex models.

rationale: The pain is genuine and the buyer (technical artist or viz engineer at a studio) is nameable and has paid for tools before — but the core bottleneck is a geometry processing problem that Claude and a prompt pipeline simply cannot solve; it requires licensed CAD kernels (Parasolid SDK alone costs thousands per seat), mesh repair algorithms, and per-model validation that a human or specialized software must perform. Operational_autonomy and buildability_with_ai both score 2 because this is fundamentally a computational geometry product, not an AI-text-automation product, making it the wrong fit for this factory. Total of 3.0 falls well below the 5.5 validate threshold.
solution_plan: This is not a viable build for a non-technical solo operator using a Claude factory. The actual solution requires licensing the Parasolid SDK or integrating Open CASCADE, writing or wrapping mesh repair algorithms, and running a GPU-capable conversion pipeline — none of which can be done with prompts, a landing page, and Stripe. A solo non-technical founder would need to hire a C++/Python geometry engineer and negotiate SDK licensing before writing a line of product code. Recommending drop: the problem is real but it is an engineering infrastructure problem, not an AI automation opportunity.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (scored 2, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai (scored 2, floor is 6). Even if total were higher, these gates would cap the stage at validate. The opportunity is dropped on total score alone (3.0 < 5.5 validate threshold), and the gate failures confirm the direction.
